claims.sourceText: Library and Archives Canada, online exhibition 'Canada's UFOs: The Search for the Unknown', Shirley's Bay / Project Magnet page, 2005
claims.text: Library and Archives Canada quotes the memorandum: '...the existence of a different technology is borne out by the investigations which are being carried on at the present time in relation to flying saucers.... I feel that the correlation between our basic theory and the available information on saucers checks too closely to be mere coincidence' (Smith, Geo-Magnetics, Department of Transport, November 21, 1950).

edges.label: 1952 recommendation to acquire the technology prefigures Condign's redacted 'Related Military Applications'
edges.note: Smith's 1952 report recommends 'acquisition of as much as possible of this technology'; Condign's own paragraph 7, 'Related Military Applications', is redacted in full under the defence exemption. Reasoning: both are government documents whose exploitation sections are the point at which the record becomes either explicit or withheld.

edges.label: author of the request that created Project Magnet
edges.note: LAC's exhibition quotes the 21 November 1950 'Geo-Magnetics' memorandum as the origin of the project.
